Developed by: BLACK HOLE STUDIO SPORTS World Test Championship 2025-27 standings:
 By Team Herald Published: 1 November 2026 Share SHARE New Zealand continue to lead the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 standings with 52 points and a points percentage of 72.22 after six matches. South Africa are close behind in second place, while Australia occupy third position.
 India are currently fourth in the table with 68 points from 11 matches. The team has recorded five wins, four defeats and two draws, giving it a points percentage of 51.52.

 South Africa have accumulated 60 points from seven matches, with five wins and two defeats. Their points percentage stands at 71.43, just below New Zealand.
 Australia, meanwhile, have played the most matches among the top four teams. With nine wins and four defeats from 13 Tests, they have collected 108 points and have a points percentage of 69.23.
 Bangladesh are fifth with 40 points and a percentage of 47.62, having won three, lost three and drawn one of their seven matches. England occupy sixth place with 74 points from 16 matches, but their points percentage is 38.54. They have also received a deduction of 14 points.
 Sri Lanka are seventh with 24 points and a percentage of 33.33, followed by West Indies in eighth place with 42 points and 26.92%. Pakistan are at the bottom of the table with five points and a points percentage of 4.63 after nine matches. They have recorded two wins and seven defeats, along with a 19-point deduction.
 - Advertisement - The standings show a closely contested race among the top three, with New Zealand, South Africa and Australia separated by relatively small differences in points percentage. India will need consistent results in their remaining matches to improve their position in the championship table.
